defects_closed.claim: $MONETA_SRC points at a live git worktree, so the memory substrate was 'whatever branch is checked out'. moneta_provenance() reported version=None (importlib.metadata has no distribution for a path-injected copy) and never the commit.
defects_closed.fix: moneta_provenance() resolves the checked-out git SHA by reading git metadata FILES (no subprocess), cached per package root, bounded walk, refuses installed copies. Reported in the deposit metadata AND carried by the Memory as a moneta_rev tag.

findings.claim: The two interpreters load DIFFERENT Moneta copies. hython 3.13.10 (the SHIPPING interpreter) has no ambient moneta, so the $MONETA_SRC fallback is the only path and the substrate IS the live C:/Users/User/Moneta/src worktree. System python 3.14.2 (the GATE interpreter) imports a pip copy from C:/Python314/Lib/site-packages/moneta and never consults $MONETA_SRC. The brief's Defect-2 premise is therefore true on the shipping interpreter and false on the gate interpreter.
findings.note: A finding written under the gate interpreter and one written under hython come from different substrates. provenance.revision + provenance.file now record which, honestly, per deposit.

findings.claim: The revision walk was unbounded, so Moneta resolved from inside ANY enclosing git repo reported that repo's HEAD as the Moneta revision. Fabricated provenance is worse than absent provenance because it is trusted.
findings.note: Found by the mutation battery, not by review. First fix (site-packages guard + MAX_REVISION_WALK=3) was INCOMPLETE - CRUCIBLE showed a vendored copy at <repo>/vendor/moneta-src/moneta still inherited the host HEAD, and the pin covering only the site-packages sub-case made the class READ closed. Bound is now 1, which covers every real layout including the deployed <repo>/src, and revision_repo names the repository that answered.

findings.claim: deposit()'s honest status reached no consumer. science/deposit.py:85 discarded the return value and backfill() returned no substrate counter, so a permanently-failing Moneta leg would have reported a clean 'N deposited' / 'N files written'. A status nobody reads is the same defect as a stub nobody calls.
findings.note: Found by CRUCIBLE. Both consumers now count and surface moneta_deposited / moneta_failures, each pinned with a positive AND a negative control.

findings.claim: 'deposited: True' did not mean durable. MonetaBackedStore.add() writes to the in-memory ECS; there is no per-deposit save, the snapshot daemon is deliberately not started, and the WAL is inert. A hard exit between deposit and teardown loses the row.
findings.note: Found by CRUCIBLE. Status now carries `durable: False` + `durability` as separate machine-readable fields rather than one field and a footnote. Survivable because the per-record JSON file is the durable source of truth - but nothing re-derives Moneta from it. See for_ruling FR2.

findings.claim: moneta_provenance() called importlib.metadata.version() on every invocation, i.e. on every ledger deposit. That scans installed-distribution metadata per call; a backfill of N records paid N scans.
findings.note: Self-review finding. Version lookup is now cached per process alongside the revision; both caches clear together so a caller cannot read a spliced provenance.

findings.claim: Moneta is append-only with no dedup key. Re-depositing the same finding yields ONE record file and TWO substrate rows sharing a Memory.id. backfill() re-run multiplies the substrate.
findings.note: Pinned as KNOWN behaviour (test_redeposit_appends_and_is_not_claimed_as_unique) rather than left to be discovered in production. See for_ruling FR5.

findings.claim: A docstring claimed the ledger store and the project store 'never contend' for Moneta's single-owner lock. False: point $SYNAPSE_LEDGER_DIR at the project storage dir and the second handle raises MonetaResourceLockedError. The separation is a property of the DEFAULT paths, not a guarantee.
findings.note: Found by CRUCIBLE. Docstring corrected to state the condition. The failure surfaces as a reported error: status and never touches the file write.

for_ruling.decision: MONETA_SRC packaging: pin Moneta to an installed artifact, or keep the worktree?
for_ruling.context: packages/synapse.json:19 sets MONETA_SRC=$SYNAPSE_ROOT/../Moneta/src. That worktree is on branch main at 2965e5dc with 2 untracked files at root (attention_log.py, test_attention_log_gil_guard.py). Checking out a branch there silently changes SYNAPSE's memory behaviour.
for_ruling.recommendation: Pin for release, keep the worktree for development - the two are not in tension if the package pins and a documented env override restores the worktree.
for_ruling.tradeoff: PIN (wheel/tag): the substrate stops moving under SYNAPSE, provenance becomes exact rather than committed-only, and the shipping interpreter stops depending on a directory that exists only on Joe's machine. COST: Moneta changes need a rebuild+reinstall to reach SYNAPSE, which slows the tight co-development loop that produced Moneta in the first place. KEEP: instant iteration. COST: the substrate backing live memory is whatever is checked out plus uncommitted edits, and the SHA this leg added narrows but cannot close that - REVISION_SCOPE says so explicitly.
for_ruling.not_taken: The brief forbids changing MONETA_SRC in this leg. Nothing was changed; this is reported only.

for_ruling.decision: Build a Moneta reconciler from the per-record files, or accept the durability gap?
for_ruling.context: LEDGER.F8. Moneta rows live in memory until close()/atexit. The per-record JSON files ARE durable and contain everything needed to rebuild, but nothing rebuilds them. A crash loses substrate rows silently while the files survive.
for_ruling.recommendation: Build it - it is a short function (walk ledger_dir, deposit each record whose Memory.id is absent) and this repo keeps a crash harness precisely because hard exits happen.
for_ruling.tradeoff: Reconciling on startup costs an O(n) scan per session. Not reconciling means recall silently under-reports findings after any crash, with no signal that it is doing so.

for_ruling.decision: Wire recall over the ledger's Moneta store, or accept enrichment without a consumer?
for_ruling.context: The seam now deposits findings into a store rooted at ledger_dir(). ledger_moneta_store() is public precisely so a reader has a named door. Today nothing reads it - synapse_recall/memory_query read the PROJECT store, a different URI.
for_ruling.recommendation: Wire it, or the seam is verified-but-unused - the same shape as the defect this leg closed, one level up.
for_ruling.tradeoff: Merging the two stores into one URI would give unified recall but reintroduces the single-owner lock contention this design avoids (LEDGER.F11). A federated read across both is the safer shape.

for_ruling.decision: Where does agent_usd_path come from for the live ledger path? (task 2.5)
for_ruling.context: LEDGER.F6. ledger.py is deliberately zero-hou, but agent.usd location is scene-scoped ($HIP). The only live producer passes nothing, so the USD projection never runs in production.
for_ruling.recommendation: Resolve it the way ledger_dir() already resolves its root - an env var with a repo-relative default - so the zero-hou contract holds.
for_ruling.tradeoff: An env-var default may point at a repo-level agent.usd rather than the scene's, which is wrong for per-scene provenance but right for a headless probe run. Picking one is a product call, not a code call.

for_ruling.decision: Accept duplicate substrate rows on re-deposit, or dedupe?
for_ruling.context: LEDGER.F10. Same finding twice = one file, two rows, same Memory.id.
for_ruling.recommendation: Accept for now and dedupe at READ time by Memory.id - a write-time check is an O(n) scan per deposit, which is the wrong cost on the hot path.
for_ruling.tradeoff: Read-time dedup keeps writes cheap but lets the substrate grow without bound across repeated backfills; the sleep pass will not prune these because ledger findings are SHOW-tier protected by design.

for_ruling.decision: Is the gate interpreter measuring the shipping substrate?
for_ruling.context: LEDGER.F1. The 4917-pass gate number was produced on python 3.14.2 against a PIP-installed Moneta. Artists run hython 3.13.10 against the MONETA_SRC worktree. The seam is proven live on both, but the suite number describes only the former.
for_ruling.recommendation: Treat this as another instance of the already-open gate-vs-shipping split recorded in suite_baseline.json, not as a new problem - but do not cite the gate number as evidence about the shipping substrate.
for_ruling.tradeoff: Adding a hython leg to the seam pins would measure the real substrate at the cost of a Houdini dependency in CI.
